# wallix.bastion.config_x509

Manage the X.509 configuration of a WALLIX Bastion — module

*Added in version 1.1.0 of `wallix.bastion`.*

## Synopsis

- Install the certificate the Bastion GUI and API serve, and configure the X.509 authentication of users.
- With [`state=absent`](#parameter-state), restore the default configuration of the Bastion (its own certificate, X.509 authentication disabled).
- Equivalent of the `wallix-bastion_config_x509` Terraform resource.
- The X.509 configuration is a singleton. The Bastion API returns the subject of the certificates, not the certificates themselves, so the module compares the common name (CN) of the certificates given with the subjects returned, like the Terraform provider does. The private key cannot be compared, see [`update_password`](#parameter-update-password).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Comments |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="parameter-api-version"></a>**api_version** | `str` | Version of the Bastion REST API to use, `v3.8` or `v3.12`.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_API_VERSION` environment variable is used, then `v3.12`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-host"></a>**bastion_host** | `str` | Hostname or IP address of the WALLIX Bastion.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_HOST` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-password"></a>**bastion_password** | `str` | Password of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PASSWORD` environment variable is used.<br>One of [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password) or [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token) is required. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-port"></a>**bastion_port** | `int` | HTTPS port of the WALLIX Bastion API.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_PORT` environment variable is used, then `443`. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-timeout"></a>**bastion_timeout** | `int` | Timeout in seconds of each HTTP request to the Bastion API.<br><br>Default: `30` |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-token"></a>**bastion_token** | `str` | API key of [`bastion_user`](#parameter-bastion-user). Takes precedence over [`bastion_password`](#parameter-bastion-password).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_TOKEN` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-bastion-user"></a>**bastion_user** | `str` | User to authenticate with. With [`bastion_token`](#parameter-bastion-token), the user the API key belongs to.<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_BASTION_USER` environment variable is used. |
| <a id="parameter-ca-certificate"></a>**ca_certificate** | `str` | Certificate, or chain, in PEM format of the authority the certificates of the users must be signed by, for X.509 authentication.<br>When the configuration is written and this option is not set, the Bastion may drop its current CA. |
| <a id="parameter-csrf-enabled"></a>**csrf_enabled** | `bool` | Send the CSRF token the Bastion issues at login (Bastion 12.0.3 and later).<br>If not set, the value of the `WALLIX_CSRF_ENABLED` environment variable is used, then `true`. |
| <a id="parameter-enable"></a>**enable** | `bool` | Whether X.509 authentication of users is enabled.<br>When unset, a change keeps the current value, or `false` when installing the configuration. |
| <a id="parameter-server-private-key"></a>**server_private_key** | `str` | Private key of [`server_public_key`](#parameter-server-public-key), in PEM format.<br>Required when [`state=present`](#parameter-state). Sent with every change. |
| <a id="parameter-server-public-key"></a>**server_public_key** | `str` | Server certificate the GUI and the API serve, in PEM format.<br>Required when [`state=present`](#parameter-state). |
| <a id="parameter-state"></a>**state** | `str` | `present` installs the configuration. `absent` restores the default one.<br><br>Choices: `present` (default), `absent` |
| <a id="parameter-update-password"></a>**update_password** | `str` | `on_create` writes the configuration only when it is not installed yet or when a compared option differs.<br>`always` writes it on every run, which then always reports a change. Use it to replace [`server_private_key`](#parameter-server-private-key) or a certificate with the same common name.<br><br>Choices: `always`, `on_create` (default) |
| <a id="parameter-validate-certs"></a>**validate_certs** | `bool` | Whether to validate the Bastion's TLS certificate.<br>Only disable this for test instances with self-signed certificates.<br>If not set, `WALLIX_BASTION_VALIDATE_CERTS` is used, then the inverse of `WALLIX_INSECURE_SKIP_VERIFY`, then `true`. |

## Attributes

| Attribute | Support | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **check_mode** | full | Can run in check_mode and return changed status prediction without modifying target. |
| **diff_mode** | full | Will return details on what has changed (or possibly needs changing in check_mode), when in diff mode. |

## Notes

- Every change restarts the HTTPS listener of the Bastion. The module waits for the API to answer again.
- Changing the certificate changes what [`validate_certs`](#parameter-validate-certs) checks. Enabling X.509 authentication may change how the API authenticates the account used by Ansible. Test on a non-production Bastion first.
- The environment variables are the ones of the `wallix/wallix-bastion` Terraform provider, so one shell configuration serves both tools.
- Set the connection options once per play with `module_defaults` and the `group/wallix.bastion.bastion` action group.
- These modules call the Bastion API from the host they run on; use them with `delegate_to` or on a play targeting `localhost`.

## Examples

```yaml
- name: Install the ACME certificate and enable X.509 authentication
  wallix.bastion.config_x509:
    server_public_key: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'cert.pem') }}"
    server_private_key: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'privkey.pem') }}"
    ca_certificate: "{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.file', 'chain.pem') }}"
    enable: true

- name: Go back to the default certificate of the Bastion
  wallix.bastion.config_x509:
    state: absent
```

## Return values

| Key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| <a id="return-changed-fields"></a>**changed_fields** | `list / elements=str` | Options that differed from the Bastion and were updated.<br><br>Returned: when [`state=present`](#parameter-state)<br><br>Sample: `["enable"]` |
| <a id="return-config-x509"></a>**config_x509** | `dict` | The X.509 configuration as returned by the Bastion API after the change, without the private key.<br>Certificates are returned as their subject.<br>In check mode, the expected configuration.<br><br>Returned: always<br><br>Sample: see [below](#sample-config-x509) |

<a id="sample-config-x509"></a>

### Sample of `config_x509`

```yaml
ca_certificate: /C=FR/O=WALLIX/CN=Users CA
default: false
enable: true
server_public_key: /C=FR/O=WALLIX/CN=bastion.example.com
```
